comparison: Strong agreement on core methodological innovation (C2, C3, C15, C18, C19). Both evaluations find the differentiable Gillespie algorithm well-supported with clear methodological description. OpenEval additionally includes C17 in its analysis. Both cite Figure 1 and affirm the conceptual leap as convincing and innovative.

Perfect agreement on future directions and limitations (C90-C97). Both evaluations classify these as appropriate speculative statements about potential extensions. OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN (未完成 work), while peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED (appropriate future directions). The difference reflects interpretation of what constitutes 'support' for forward-looking claims.

Strong agreement on benchmarking results (C38, C40, C41, C44, C45, C46, C85, C86). Both acknowledge accuracy for bulk properties and documented limitations for distribution tails. OpenEval additionally includes C33, C34, C37, C47 in this result. Both evaluations accept the nuanced picture of successes and limitations as well-supported.

Partial overlap on limitations (C33, C34, C37). OpenEval groups these limitation claims with broader benchmarking results (R2), while peer reviewers evaluate them separately. Both find the acknowledged limitations appropriately documented rather than problematic, treating them as accepted trade-offs.

Strong agreement on core capability enabled by differentiability (C83, C84). Both evaluations affirm this as a fundamental strength with broad potential impact. OpenEval additionally includes C88 in this result. Peer reviewers emphasize potential for driving innovations in biochemical network analysis.

Agreement on parameter estimation challenges (C53, C54, C55, C56). Both evaluations accept findings about loss landscape flatness and parameter degeneracy. OpenEval groups these with broader capability claims (C4, C6, C16, C87), while peer reviewers focus specifically on the landscape analysis. Both cite Figures 5 and 6 as supporting evidence.

Strong agreement on circuit design capability (C5, C7, C75, C89). Both evaluations affirm the demonstrated ability to design promoter architectures with desired input-output relationships. OpenEval additionally includes C73, C74, C81, C82 connecting to nonequilibrium design principles. Both cite Figure 8 as comprehensive supporting evidence.

Partial agreement on parameter estimation capability (C4, C6, C87). OpenEval groups these capability statements with detailed landscape analysis (R3), while peer reviewers evaluate the general capability separately with some caveats about inference reliability. Both mark as SUPPORTED but peer review notes need for multiple random initializations.

Agreement on experimental validation results (C69, C70, C72). Both evaluations accept the quantitative error metrics and strong agreement for r/γ ratio. OpenEval groups these with broader experimental validation claims (C20, C58, C66-C68), while peer reviewers focus on the specific quantitative results without challenge.

Agreement on biological interpretations (C66, C67, C68). OpenEval includes these in broader experimental validation result (R4), while peer reviewers note these biological inferences are not challenged. Both implicitly accept these as reasonable conclusions from parameter estimation.

Disagreement on nonequilibrium design claims (C82). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED with citations to theoretical work, while peer reviewer marks as UNCERTAIN, raising specific concern about sharpness values falling below equilibrium limit (0.25), suggesting potential misinterpretation of cited work (Lammers & Flamholz 2023).

Minimal overlap on impact assessment (C88). OpenEval includes robustness and impact assessment in core capability result (R6), while peer reviewers briefly mention potential impact in their parameter estimation evaluation (R4). Both are positive but emphasize different aspects.

Minimal overlap on optimization capability (C47). OpenEval includes this as bridge claim in benchmarking result (R2), while peer reviewers mention it briefly in parameter estimation context (R4). Both accept the capability but don't emphasize it.

OpenEval evaluates model system rationale (C48, C49, C50) as SUPPORTED background knowledge with proper citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate the choice of benchmark system.

OpenEval evaluates background context claims (C1, C8-C14) about stochastic processes and Gillespie algorithm as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately assess background literature claims.
